I am a 50-year-old farmer from Quzhou County. I have been farming this land for over 30 years. My family has about 8 mu of good flat land on the North China Plain, and I know this soil well. Every year, I follow the wheat-maize double-cropping system that all my neighbors use — it is the only way to make full use of our land and water.

This year, I will plant winter wheat on all 8 mu in early October, and then plant summer maize right after the wheat harvest in early June. That is what I always do. The wheat gives me a stable base, and the maize gives me a second harvest. I cannot afford to leave the land idle.

For the wheat, I will use rotary tillage before sowing to break up the soil after the maize harvest. I will sow about 30 jin of improved wheat seed per mu — I like varieties like Luyuan 502 or Jimai 22. They are reliable. I will put down about 100 jin of compound fertilizer as basal dressing — the 18-22-5 type from the local supply store — and then top-dress with urea at the jointing stage. All together that is about 65 kg of nitrogen, 22 kg of phosphate, and 8 kg of potash per mu. I will irrigate three times: once at sowing, once at the winter irrigation around New Year, and once at the jointing stage in spring. I also need to spray pesticides about four times — herbicide once at the early stage, insecticide twice for aphids and other pests, and fungicide once to prevent rust. If the weather cooperates, I expect about 1,000 kg of wheat per mu.

For the maize, after I harvest the wheat in early June, I will use no-tillage direct seeding — there is no time to waste in the summer season. I will plant about 1.2 jin of hybrid maize seed per mu, usually Denghai 605. It is a good hybrid with strong stalks. I will apply about 80 jin of 28-6-6 compound fertilizer at sowing, which gives roughly 24 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphate, and 6 kg potash per mu. I will irrigate twice — once right after sowing and once at the big喇叭口 stage. For pests, I will spray herbicide once and insecticide twice, so three pesticide applications in total. The maize should yield about 1,100 kg per mu if there is no bad storm.

I keep some grain for family use and feeding, and sell the rest. Last year's prices were decent. I will stick with this plan because it has fed my family for decades.
